title: Trump's Space Transportation Policy Aims to Expand US Spaceport Infrastructure for Surge in Launches
summary: The Trump administration's new national space transportation policy focuses on expanding US spaceport infrastructure to support over 1,000 launches and reentries annually by 2030. Key updates include prioritizing infrastructure investments, improving range scheduling transparency, identifying new federal land for spaceports, and enhancing geographic resiliency with additional heavy-lift launch sites. The policy also emphasizes responsive launch operations and commercial missions to the Moon and Mars.
key_points: The policy replaces a 2013 directive, reflecting the significant growth in the launch sector (e.g., 176 US orbital launches in 2023 vs. ~18 in 2013).
Targets over 1,000 launches/reentries per year by 2030, driven by commercial and military demand for communications, surveillance, and orbital data centers.
Directs the Pentagon and NASA to coordinate infrastructure investments to boost capacity at federal spaceports (e.g., Cape Canaveral, Vandenberg, Wallops).
Calls for transparent range scheduling to optimize launch capacity and balance commercial/government needs.
Identifies federal lands for new spaceports, including potential offshore sites using abandoned oil rigs.
Supports a third heavy-lift launch site for geographic resiliency, as recommended by a Pentagon study.
Encourages responsive launch operations (e.g., 48-hour payload deployment) and portable launch infrastructure.
Aligns with NASA’s commercial lunar/Mars transportation goals and ongoing efforts to streamline permitting and user fees.
